# Capability catalog

Read this before you build. Every unit in titan-platform is listed with what it is for, when
to reach for it, and its main exports. If a unit already does what you need, use it. If one
almost fits, file a task naming the missing export (see
[where code goes](https://hjewkes.github.io/titan-platform/guides/where-code-goes)). Then check the runtime paths: the credential a
path needs decides whether it works where your job runs.

Before adding code:

1. Read this catalog and the reference page of every unit that looks close.
2. Name the existing unit you reuse, or the gap you fill and its task.
3. Verify runtime and auth assumptions with the path's smoke check before you build on them.

## Proven runtime paths

Each path below runs a model or an external tool. Check the credential before you design
around a path, and run its smoke check in the environment the job will really use.

| Path | Package | Credential it needs | Smoke check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Agent SDK: `runAgent`, `createClaudeCodeAdapter` | `agent` | `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in the environment. `assertAuthEnvOk` refuses to start without it, and strips `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` unless `allowApiKeyBilling` is set. This is `runAgent`'s default harness. | A one-turn `runAgent` call with `maxTurns: 1` and a small `maxBudgetUsd`; an `auth_misconfigured` failure means the token is missing. |
| Headless `claude -p`: `runAgent({ harness: "claude-print" })` | `agent` | The Claude Code CLI's own keychain login. No OAuth token; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is stripped unless `allowApiKeyBilling` is set. One turn only: tools, MCP, hooks and resume throw a `TypeError` before spawn. Not yet a `HarnessAdapter`, so `dispatchHarnessRun` and the durable dispatcher cannot use it. | A one-turn `runAgent({ harness: "claude-print", model: "sonnet", prompt, outputSchema, maxTurns: 1, maxBudgetUsd: 0.5 })`; a logged-out CLI returns `auth_misconfigured`. |
| Codex exec: `createCodexExecAdapter({ auth: "cached-cli" })` | `agent` | A cached `codex login` (ChatGPT). API-key variables are stripped from the child. checkCodexAvailable resolves the installed CLI, requires >=0.162.1 and checks required command capabilities; availability is not a login or permission certificate. | `TITAN_SMOKE_MODEL=<model> pnpm smoke:codex --run` |
| Workflow step runners: `agentRunner`, `durableHarnessRunner`, `idempotentRunner`, `inlineRunner` | `workflow` | `agentRunner` calls `runAgent`, so it needs `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, or only the CLI login when its `defaults` set `harness: "claude-print"`. `durableHarnessRunner` needs whatever its dispatcher's adapter needs. `inlineRunner` needs nothing; `idempotentRunner` wraps another runner. | Run the workflow once with `inlineRunner` to prove the steps, then swap in the model runner. |
| Autoresearch ports: `ArPorts` (`pin`, `plan`, `allocTree`, `implement`, `staticCheck`, `micro`, `evalCase`, `ratchet`, `releaseTree`) | `autoresearch` | No credential in the package. It never calls a model, a shell or git itself; every effect is a port the host supplies, so the host's ports carry whatever the implementer agent and the evaluator need (see the `agent` paths above). | `pnpm vitest run packages/autoresearch` runs the whole recipe on fake ports over a local fixture repo and bare remote, at $0 and with no model call. |
| Style tool runners: ESLint, ruff, and the Python audit tools | `style-checker` | No credential. ESLint runs through `npx` and needs its plugins installed. ruff, `lint-imports`, vulture, pydoclint and pyright must be on PATH; an absent Python audit tool returns a warning naming its `pip install`, never a throw. | `ruff --version` and `npx eslint --version` in the target repo. |
| Embedding backends: `local`, `ollama`, hash fallback | `embed` | No credential. `local` needs the optional `@huggingface/transformers` peer; `ollama` needs a reachable Ollama. `fallbackToHash: true` keeps a run alive with neither. | `createEmbedder({ backend: "ollama" }, { fallbackToHash: true, onFallback: console.warn })`; a warning means the hash fallback took over. |
| agent-chat CLI: roster read, reviewer spawn, resume (`agent ls --json`, `agent spawn <name> <profile> --brief-stdin`, `agent resume <name> --message <text>`) | `agent-dispatch` | No credential in the caller. The agent-chat broker starts `claude` under its own login or the profile's config dir. The CLI reaches the broker over its 0600 unix socket as the same OS user, so a broker must be running; set `AGENT_CHAT_NO_AUTOSTART=1` to fail instead of starting one. A spawn runs in the caller's cwd. | `AGENT_CHAT_NO_AUTOSTART=1 agent-chat agent ls --json` prints a JSON array (about 6.5 s with 700 rows, so do not call it on a hot path). Then `printf 'Reply with the word ok and stop.' \| agent-chat agent spawn <name> <profile> --brief-stdin`; the roster row ends with `presence: "exited"`, a non-empty `sessionId` and `transcriptExists: true`. Resume, smoke-tested 2026-10-06: once that row has exited, `agent-chat agent resume <name> --message <text>` runs a new turn in the same session; `sessionId` is the same before and after, and both replies are in one transcript. |

under its task instead of inside a product. Edit the list in `scripts/capabilities-data.json`.

| TP-226 | `agent` | No `claude -p` adapter with a pinned conversation id |

| TP-147 | `messaging` | No channel-neutral inbound, liveness or capabilities |
| TP-150 | `messaging` | No Web Push backend |
| TP-118 | `session-read` | No storage-free `tailTranscript(path, turns)` read-back helper |

| TP-309 | `code-graph` | `computeLcomMetrics` and cognitive complexity are not exported from the root |
| TP-166 | `code-parser` | `.tsx` files parse with the TypeScript grammar, and `.js` has no grammar |
| TP-189 | `style-profile` | `generateEslintExport` emits a config without plugins, parser or files |
| TP-235 | `style-profile` | Generated naming-convention config passes values typescript-eslint rejects |
| TP-358 | `docs` | Some package.json descriptions are stale, and they feed this catalog |

## Tier 0 — primitives

Domain-free building blocks. No titan dependencies.

<a id="cap-agent-protocol"></a>

### [`agent-protocol`](https://hjewkes.github.io/titan-platform/reference/agent-protocol)

Tier 0, `@titan-design/agent-protocol@0.9.1`. Harness-neutral identity and usage contracts for execution and session readers

**Use this when:**

You need identity, execution-phase or usage types that stay the same whichever harness (Claude Code or Codex) ran the work. For a canonical, zod-validated execution-trace record (run, attempt, call, gate, artifact, cost) with a privacy redactor, import `./trace`. To count usage without double-counting deltas and snapshots, call `foldUsage`.

For SDK-free execution targets, capability/limit assessments and generic progress/result/failure contracts and transcript source/observation/continuation DTOs, import ./harness; native execution stays in agent.

HarnessSourcePort describes injected discovery, scoped lookup and semantic observation/text reads; its capability assessments preserve unsupported/unverified operations without providing runtime adapters or finality guarantees.

HarnessExecutionPort adds an open generic execution service with profile/account/billing-pool binding references, model/output intent, an interface version and distinct dispatch receipts. These structural contracts add no runtime validation, authenticated authority or qualified native capability; account/quota, policy and bus ports remain pending.

HarnessPricingPort describes an event-time quote with optional readonly normalized cache-write TTL context: reported cost, a source-provided existing estimate, a dated/versioned catalog estimate with matching/accounting policy references, or explicit unpriced reason. It supplies no arithmetic, catalog or provider adapter.

For shared dated pricing and cost arithmetic, import `./pricing`; its existing Claude TTL/long-prompt and Codex inclusive-token accounting engines preserve compatibility entrypoints without native account reads or stored-cost rewrites.

For zod schemas of agent-chat's spawn, resume, retire, agents and surface frames and the records they carry, import `./wire`.

Key exports:

- `lifecycle`: `EXECUTION_PHASES`, `TERMINAL_EXECUTION_PHASES`
- `lifecycle-correlations`: `CORRELATION_KEY_PATTERN`, `MAX_CORRELATION_VALUE_LENGTH`, `correlationKey`, `validateCorrelations`
- `lifecycle-validation`: `ExecutionTransitionError`
- `lifecycle-reducer`: `isTerminalExecutionPhase`, `reduceExecutionTransition`
- `usage-fold`: `foldUsage`
- `index`: `conversationRef`, `conversationItemRef`
- More in the [reference page](https://hjewkes.github.io/titan-platform/reference/agent-protocol)

<a id="cap-anthropic-account"></a>

### [`anthropic-account`](https://hjewkes.github.io/titan-platform/reference/anthropic-account)

Tier 0, `@titan-design/anthropic-account@0.3.0`. Anthropic account state: usage readings, token-free login state, account labels and secret redaction, with a ./node subpath for profiles, the 0600-gated credentials read, the usage file, the usage poller and the locked, atomic token refresh

**Use this when:**

You need to read a Claude Code account's state without touching a token: parse a status-line usage reading with `parseUsageReading`, map the OAuth usage endpoint's response into that shape with `usageFromOAuthResponse`, turn a parsed `.credentials.json` object into a token-free `LoginState` with `loginStateFromCredentials` and `needsRefresh`, name an account from its config dir with `accountLabel`, or scrub tokens from a log line or an Error with `redactSecrets`. The root is pure code. The `./node` subpath does the file work: `discoverProfiles` lists the config dirs, `readLoginState` reads a credentials file only when it is a regular file of mode 0600 or narrower owned by the caller, `readUsage` and `writeReading` read the newest reading and atomically write `usage-poll.json`, and `pollUsage` and `pollAll` fetch a fresh reading from the OAuth usage endpoint through an injected `fetch`, never refreshing a token. `refreshIfNeeded` is the one writer of credentials: it renews a due access token under Claude Code's refresh lock, replaces `.credentials.json` atomically without overwriting another writer, and hands each failure to an `onFailure` callback as an owner-queue deposit. The `anthropic-account` bin runs `poll [--write [--refresh]]` from a systemd user timer (templates in `systemd/`, installed by hand) and `status [--json|--statusline]` for the status line and the pace pass; an expired or refused login exits 2, and `poll` skips a profile with no login or one backing off after a 429. For the harness-neutral usage and cost types of an agent run use `agent-protocol` instead.

Key exports:

- `usage`: `POLL_SESSION_ID`, `POLL_SOURCE`, `parseUsageReading`, `usageFromOAuthResponse`, `OAuthUsageOptions`, `UsageReading`
- `login`: `loginStateFromCredentials`, `needsRefresh`
- `profile`: `DEFAULT_LABEL`, `accountLabel`
- `redact`: `REDACTED`, `redactSecrets`
- More in the [reference page](https://hjewkes.github.io/titan-platform/reference/anthropic-account)

<a id="cap-fix-proof"></a>

### [`fix-proof`](https://hjewkes.github.io/titan-platform/reference/fix-proof)

Tier 0, `@titan-design/fix-proof@0.8.0`. Proves a fix PR's new tests fail on the merge base and pass at head: diff plan, vitest report classification, fix-proof/v1 result line

**Use this when:**

You must decide whether a fix pull request's added or changed tests fail on the merge base and pass at head. It plans the overlay from a `git diff -M --name-status` and the base config, classifies two vitest JSON reports per test into a `reproduced`, `unproven`, `vacuous`, `no-tests` or `error` verdict, and encodes it as a 4 KB `fix-proof/v1` line. For a tests-only diff it also tells test material from source (`testOnlyOf`) and parses `*.mutations.json` specs, and `classifyMutants` decides whether every declared mutation was killed, which the judge adds to the line as `mutants`. Its `fix-proof exec` bin builds and tests one side in a git worktree and writes encoded reports, and `exec --side mutants` runs each declared mutation against the merge base in the sandbox; `fix-proof judge` (also `dist/judge.js`) decodes them, runs only git and prints that line, so CI can keep PR-head code out of the job that prints the verdict. To read where a fix-proof read leaves a head (proved, NO_REPRO, unverified, unproven or none), call `proofStanding` and ask it `endsReview` or `needsTestsSeat`; do not parse the line again. `execHeadMutants` runs generated mutations (`HeadMutation`, no `kills`) against head, each against its owning package's suite, and classifies each as `survived`, `caught`, `caught-error`, `load-error` or `timeout`, for audits that look for covered but untested code. To decide who may merge afterwards, use authority.

A package compiles globs or other untrusted patterns to a RegExp: construct a `LinearRegExp` from `@titan-design/fix-proof/linear-regexp` in place of `new RegExp`, so matching cannot backtrack polynomially; its tests count `linearRegExpSteps()` instead of timing it.

Key exports:

- `config`: `isHarnessPath`, `parseFixProofConfig`
- `glob`: `compileGlobs`, `expandBraces`
- `linear-regexp`: `LinearRegExp`, `linearRegExpSteps`
- `plan`: `planFixProof`, `testOnlyOf`, `testOnlyReading`
- `mutation`: `checkMutation`, `parseMutationSpec`
- `mutant-classify`: `classifyMutants`
- More in the [reference page](https://hjewkes.github.io/titan-platform/reference/fix-proof)

**Use this when:**

You need token-free Codex account state from an explicit CODEX_HOME: parse `codex login status`, validate rollout token_count rate_limits evidence and refuse admission when its observation freshness cannot be verified. Native rollouts return unknown/freshness-unverified; quota age and numerical admission policy require a caller-established known observation. The pure root exports `loginStateFromStatus`, `usageFromRolloutEvents`, `quotaAdmission`, `accountLabel` and `redactSecrets`; `./node` exposes the bounded login probe and read-only rollout scan. It never reads auth.json or provisions an account. For Claude account state use anthropic-account; for execution and transcript decoding use agent and session-read.

Use `knownObservation` to explicitly attest a quota observation time source before admission; plain or serialized known readings do not carry that process-local provenance. The factory does not authenticate a backend or account.

Tier 0, `@titan-design/owner-proof@0.1.0`. Owner-signed statements: canonical JSON, P-256 key ring and an exact-bytes ECDSA verify core generic over a zod schema

**Use this when:**

You must accept an action only when the owner signed a statement for it with an ECDSA P-256 key (such as the Secure Enclave key behind Touch ID). `verifySigned` checks the DER signature over the exact received bytes against a `keyRing` of installed public keys before it parses anything, then the zod schema, the issue and expiry window, the audience and your statement kind's own checks; `canonical` gives sorted-key JSON for digests. It keeps no state, so nonce replay is yours to record. To decide which actions need the owner at all, use authority.

Key exports:

<a id="cap-github"></a>

### [`github`](https://hjewkes.github.io/titan-platform/reference/github)

Tier 1, `@titan-design/github@0.11.0`. GitHub REST port over the gh CLI: validated paths, required checks from branch rules, and an in-memory fake

**Use this when:**

Code must read or change GitHub (refs, files, pull requests, required checks, check runs, job logs, merges, reruns, branch deletes) over REST through the caller's `gh` login, with every write safe to repeat after a crash and polling paced by ETags and a shared rate budget. `mergeReadiness` decides, without I/O, whether a PR may merge at an approved head. A long-running service uses `octokitWire()` on `sharedOctokit()`: the same port, with one throttled, GET-only-retry budget per process. Use `fakeGitHub()` in tests instead of stubbing `gh`. `formatSquashMessage` (and the `titan-squash-message` bin) builds a deterministic, trailer- and email-free squash commit message from a PR and its commits. `ciVerdict` and `ciWait` (and `titan-gh ci-wait`) judge or wait on a sha's CI over the base branch's required contexts. A shell or agent reading one PR uses `titan-gh pr-status` and `titan-gh pr-context` instead of `gh pr view --json` piped to `jq`.

**Use this when:**

To serve the health route itself, use daemon. The `./metrics` subpath adds `validateEntry(entry, "write" | "read")` and the zod schemas for `titan.metrics/v1` registry entries and `titan.measurement-audit/v1` audit reports (write refuses unknown keys, read keeps them); use it to author or load a system's metric registry.

Tier 1, `@titan-design/speech-stt@0.1.0`. Speech-recognition helpers: a transformers.js Whisper recogniser with an audio-hash cache, a wav2vec2 phone recogniser with CTC logits, a CPython-parity SequenceMatcher, script alignment, transcript diff, Word and Transcript schemas, and a resampler

**Use this when:**

You compare a script with what a recogniser heard, or port Python that calls `difflib`: a CPython-parity `SequenceMatcher` and `roundHalfEven` (Python's `round`), `align` to time script words from a transcript, `diff` and `normalize` to score a take, the `Word` and `Transcript` schemas, and a pure TS `resample` (24 kHz to 16 kHz without ffmpeg). `whisperStt` transcribes audio to word-timed `Transcript`s through transformers.js Whisper (optional peer), cached by audio hash, and declares `capabilities.tokenLogprobs: true` (word probabilities and per-window segment confidence from token log-probs; opt out with `tokenLogprobs: false`). `wav2vec2Recognizer` gives espeak-style IPA phones per 20 ms frame (fp32 by default, at parity with the PyTorch model; q8 opt-in changes verdicts) and exposes the CTC logits for forced alignment. `alignWords` force-aligns a script to those logits for word starts within a frame or two, with a per-voice-family offset. Synthesis is `speech-tts`.

Key exports:

- `align`: `align`
- `diff`: `diff`, `normalize`
- `resample`: `resample`
- `round`: `roundHalfEven`
- `schemas`: `SegmentSchema`, `TranscriptSchema`, `WordSchema`

It ships an in-process Kokoro provider (fp32, misaki phonemes, word timings from the model's own durations; `unknownWords: "fail"` rejects text with unphonemized words via `TtsUnknownWordsError` instead of timing them at zero width) and helpers to tune speed to a words-per-minute target. `detectSpeechRuntime` picks each speech model's device (CPU by default, CUDA reported but opt-in) and cache directory from the platform, `TITAN_SPEECH_*` env and the profile, for speech-tts and speech-stt alike. Recognition and alignment are not here; they belong to speech-stt.

<a id="cap-worktree"></a>

### [`worktree`](https://hjewkes.github.io/titan-platform/reference/worktree)

Tier 1, `@titan-design/worktree@0.3.0`. Git worktree mechanics for headless agents: budgeted allocation, release safety, park, re-create and sweep

**Use this when:**

You give each headless agent its own git worktree and branch under a per-repository budget, and must never lose its commits: allocation adopts a crashed agent's branch, release and park refuse a tree with uncommitted or unpushed work, and a sweep finds trees nobody released. Its git and setup children preserve the existing dispatcher transport-list pin. Inputs are plain records; optional allocation groups and name-aware budgets preserve the caller's capacity policy. Requested origin-branch checkouts retain default-branch setup trust, and a branch-keeping release completes only a parked allocation. The caller keeps its own roster, journal and optional setup adapter. Launching the agent process is agent-surface; deciding which isolation strategy applies is agent-dispatch.

An explicit releaseProof opt-in recognizes the exact merged PR tip or its commit membership while retaining git-only defaults and every file-loss/nonforced-removal guard.

Failed releases expose an optional ordinary-changes code, and missing assigned allocation records have a typed error, so products can retain their wording without parsing diagnostics or changing safety.

Use fetchDefaultTip when a caller must refuse an unavailable origin instead of falling back to local HEAD; its existing fetch shares one timeout budget across default-branch candidates.

Key exports:

- `allocator`: `createWorktreeAllocator`
- `branch-base`: `fetchDefaultTip`, `resolveBranchBase`, `resolveRequestedBase`

<a id="cap-coordinator"></a>

### [`coordinator`](https://hjewkes.github.io/titan-platform/reference/coordinator)

Tier 2, `@titan-design/coordinator@0.5.3`. Seat config and charter policy schemas for the autonomy coordinator (pure code: zod schemas and inferred types).

**Use this when:**

You need to validate or type a seat's front matter (`autonomy-seat/v1`): name, prefix, pool, config dir, concurrency, spend, repos. Pure zod schema and inferred types; it reads no files and talks to no broker, so parse the front matter in the host and hand the object over. For the host that loads and runs seats, use the product that owns it, not this package. Fold a seat's event log (spawn, retire, teleport, claim, release, hold, unhold, background, authored) into `SeatState` with `foldSeatEvents`: it never throws, counts unknown kinds and refuses background commands in temp or scratchpad space. Validate the charter front matter (`autonomy-charter/v1`: seats, hub, hard stops, scorer defaults; pools and funds pass through untyped) with `parseCharterPolicy`: it never throws and returns the typed policy or errors that name the missing or invalid key path. Validate a whole `titan-coordinator/v1` document (owner, repos, seats, limits, policy) with `checkCoordinatorConfig`: it reuses the seat, charter and agent-dispatch limits schemas, never throws, and names the key path of each cross-reference error (unknown pool, repo or hard stop, duplicate prefix, seat `config_dir`, not exactly one attended seat). Project one seat generation to a `SessionFacts` record per initiative with `projectSeatGeneration`: merged PRs, closed tasks and filed tasks, mapped by task-id prefix; it is given the activity and drops work no scope claims. Validate and render the seat's authored handoff block (continuations, standing rules with expiry, open questions, next/why; at most 1,500 characters) with `parseAuthored` and `renderAuthored`. Edit a `titan-coordinator/v1` document through a revision log: `applyEdit` sets one schema-declared field on a copy and refuses an undeclared path or a result that fails `checkCoordinatorConfig`, `diffDocuments` lists changed leaves, and `verifyChain` refuses a log whose revision does not name the previous revision's `revisionSha` as its parent. Check a proposed config edit against the allowlist `EDITABLE_FIELDS` (path pattern, bounds, reload class) with `checkEditableValue`; a path no row matches is not editable.

Key exports:

- `charter-policy`: `charterDefaultsSchema`, `charterPolicyErrorSchema`, `charterPolicySchema`, `hardStopClassSchema`, `parseCharterPolicy`

### [`owner-queue`](https://hjewkes.github.io/titan-platform/reference/owner-queue)

Tier 2, `@titan-design/owner-queue@0.5.0`. The owner queue core: one OwnerItem schema across every store of record, the QueueSource port, merge-by-keys and rank as pure functions

**Use this when:**

You gather the things only the owner can answer from several stores of record (chat questions, hitl gates, task notes, review rounds) into one list and need one `OwnerItem` shape, a `QueueSource` port for adapters, a merge that joins duplicates only on an exact shared key including a PR's head sha, a deterministic rank, and pure stale rules that label an item gone elsewhere from source facts (PR merged, head moved, task done, asker retired), and `buildOwnerRounds`, which turns open Decide items into titan-review round@2 manifests with `Principle:` batching and shadow-mode picks revealed only after the answer, plus `fromRoundQuestions`/`answeredFromFeedback` to read a round's questions and feedback back as OwnerItems, and `ask:`/`component:`/`token:`/`topic:` relation keys that relate items without merging them, and `consolidate`, which turns the open queue into the approvals Flow (per-PR and topic groups, influence order, holds, and a per-PR `shipBlockedBy` from open change requests), and an optional `audience` (owner or operator) with the `forAudience` reader filter, and owner card fields (`class`, `irreversible`, `shown`, `default`, `onSilence`, option `consequence`) checked by `cardLint`/`ownerCardSchema`. The root export holds no I/O; the one exception is the `/spool` subpath, the 0600 file spool where agents file deposits and the console keeps the owner's answers. Other adapters live in the product, the gate itself is hitl, routing is decider, and mirroring to Matrix is queue-mirror.

<a id="cap-speech-vet"></a>

### [`speech-vet`](https://hjewkes.github.io/titan-platform/reference/speech-vet)

Tier 2, `@titan-design/speech-vet@0.1.0`. Speech text vetting: pronunciation override markup, heteronym reading checks, lexicon.v1, initialism spelling, number normalization and phone-level pronunciation verdicts

**Use this when:**

You hold narration text and must say how its hard words are read before any audio exists: `[word](/phonemes/)` overrides and `[word](=reading)` declarations, a heteronym check of G2P tokens against those declarations, a `lexicon.v1` file of rewrites, respellings and phonemes, dotted-letter initialisms, and `normalize()`, composable steps that spell out numbers, decimals, currency, ordinals, clock times and per-unit rates. Once audio exists, `chunkWordVerdicts`, `detectHallucinations` and `detectTailArtifact` judge a recognizer's phones against espeak-style expected phones (a port of the audiobook phone check, at verdict parity). `espeakCliG2p` supplies those expected phones by running the espeak-ng binary you install (GPL, called as a process, not bundled); `misakiIpaG2p` supplies them from speech-g2p with no binary. `checkHeardReadings` checks each declared heteronym reading against the recognized phones, espeak-free, through an injected misaki-to-IPA map. `synthesizeVerified` re-rolls babbled takes, and `keepTake`, `regressions` and `bestTailTake` choose between a shipped take and a regenerated one without shipping a worse take. `detectDefects` and `confirmDefects` find mangled, dropped and muddy words by aligning source text against a speech-stt transcript (a port of the audiobook defect check, at output parity); pass `defectOptionsFor(stt)` so the recogniser's confidence is used only when its provider has token log-probs. `vet()` composes all of it into the full cycle over injected providers (precheck, synthesize, transcribe, check, retake, keep the best take) and returns `accepted`, `needs-override`, `needs-rewrite`, `retakes-exhausted` or `stopped`; it does not normalize or search for overrides. `rewriteLine` answers `needs-rewrite` on a text voice: it replaces only the flagged sentence, resolves a pinned sentence from `RewritePins` (a hash-keyed `rewrites.json`) without asking any source, never rewrites a pinned rewrite, runs every candidate from the `symbolRules` rule tier or an injected LLM `CandidateSource` through `guardRewrite` (numbers, names, markup, content terms, length), and pins only one that re-vets `accepted`. It loads no model; tokens, phones and transcripts come from the caller. Synthesis belongs to speech-tts.

Key exports:

- `markup`: `g2pText`, `plainText`
- `heteronyms`: `checkReadings`, `englishHeteronyms`, `HeteronymTableSchema`, `readingOf`, `tokenDump`
- `lexicon`: `LexiconEntrySchema`, `LexiconSchema`, `loadLexicon`, `respellingsOf`
- `respell`: `generateCandidates`
- More in the [reference page](https://hjewkes.github.io/titan-platform/reference/speech-vet)

Tier product, `@titan-design/active-work@0.24.4`. Durable workspace state for engineering work — CLI, MCP, and Claude skill for tracking initiatives across sessions

**Use this when:**

You want durable per-initiative state (brief, tasks, sessions, artifacts, notes) that Claude Code sessions read and write through the `active-work` CLI, its MCP server or its loopback daemon, or `aw <slug>` to launch a session with the initiative's bootstrap prompt. Other products reach it over that process boundary. To validate a task record without the product, use `pm`; to resolve its data root, use `app-paths`.

Key exports:

No library entry point.

<a id="cap-corpus-query"></a>

### `corpus-query`

Tier product, private, `products/corpus-query`. Cheap one-line questions over a large local text corpus: deterministic index and retrieval, verified judge calls

**Use this when:**

You need to answer "list every X" over a large local text corpus without feeding the corpus to a model. `corpus-query index <root>` builds a per-user paragraph index: `indexCorpus` walks the files, `CorpusLayout` (`archiveLayout`, `plainLayout`) names and orders each document, `parseHeader` reads its `KEY: value` header, and `splitParagraphs` gives UTF-8 byte ranges that `SpanFtsTables` indexes contentlessly, so the index holds tokens and locators but no prose and `readSpanText` re-reads a paragraph from its file. A re-run re-indexes only files whose sha-256 changed. `QuerySpecSchema` is the shape of a compiled question. `corpus-query ask` wires the judge calls as durable `workflow` runs (`ask`, `resume`): screen on haiku, a haiku redo and then a sonnet fallback before a batch is recorded unjudged, grow to a fixed point, confirm per book, all through bare `claude-print` calls. Rendering is not here yet; ranked search over embeddings is `retrieval`, and the span index itself is `store-sqlite`.

Key exports:

- `cli`: `runCli`, `defaultIndexPath`, `formatHit`, `formatStats`
- `header`: `parseHeader`, `splitTitle`
- `index-corpus`: `chapterOwnerRef`, `indexCorpus`, `listChapters`, `migrateIndex`, `openSpans`, `readSpanText`
- More in `products/corpus-query/src/index.ts`

<a id="cap-evals"></a>

### `evals`

Tier product, private, `products/evals`. Eval registry: spec schemas for units, variants, cases, suites, checks and scorecards, with canonical content hashing

**Use this when:**

You need a stable content hash for a unit of work, a workflow variant, an eval case, a suite or a scorecard key, or strict and loose zod parsing of those specs. Also builds the labelled review outcome corpus (one row per reviewed head) from the factory database, read-only, and git history. For retrieval quality use retrieval-eval instead.

- `spec`: `CheckSpecSchema`, `EvalCaseSchema`, `ScorecardSchema`, `SuiteSpecSchema`, `UnitSpecSchema`, `TrialRecordSchema`, `VariantSpecSchema`, `parseSpec`, `parseTrialRecord`
- `hash`: `canonicalJson`, `caseHash`, `hashCanonical`
- More in `products/evals/src/index.ts`

<a id="cap-explainer"></a>

### `explainer`

Tier product, private, `products/explainer`. Explainer video pipeline: beats.json and digest.json schemas, packet builder, finding attribution

**Use this when:**

You are building a step of the explainer video pipeline and need its file contracts or its pure helpers.
`StoryboardSchema` validates `beats.json` (video type, chapters, beats with stops in seconds),
`DigestSchema` validates `digest.json`,
`LexiconSchema` and `lexiconEntriesFor` cover pronunciations,
`buildPacket` builds one beat builder's packet (throws on a code beat with no excerpt and on a packet over its byte cap), and
`attributeFindings` maps gate findings to the beat each names by beat number.
`claimsCheckWith(facts)` (Q-E20) checks each pull request, task and count a script names against the gathered facts.
`spokenTokenCheckWith(lexicon)` (Q-V14) fails a spoken line with a print device, or a path, code token, unit or acronym that no lexicon entry or phoneme override voices.
`assertionCheckWith(tagger)` (Q-D7) fails a beat headline with no subject and finite verb, over ten words, or written after its narration.
Only `explainer eval l1`, `l2`, `cold`, `items` and `smoke` and `explainer rewrite` (and `rewrite measure`) call a model, through the judge a config file names.
`explainer rewrite` (`rewriteScript`) rewrites a drafted script's spoken lines toward the Q-V11 register bands, one call per chapter a round,
keeps a beat's rewrite only when `guardBeat` accepts it,
moves extra numbers to `visual.labels`, and
with `--speech-vet` lets a vetted 26-32 word sentence through.
`explainer rewrite measure` runs it n times per input and reports each target row's mean, sd and n against the revised done-when, under a spend cap.
Only these touch the filesystem:
the eval store,
the CLI,
the owner kit,
`loadDoctrine`,
`loadProfiles`,
`loadBeatSystems`,
`writeTypeGuides`,
`gatherReview`,
`enrichStructure`,
`gatherDaily`,
`readTaskSnapshot`,
`gatherPr` and
the PR trigger.
Motion primitives and beat components live in `@titan-design/react-ui`, not here; citation checks live in `evidence`.
`lintMapBeats`, `lintMapCues` and `compileMapTimeline` check and time the repo-map track (`visual.map_state`, optional per beat), and
`toDiagramMapTimeline` turns it into titan-design's `MapTimeline` keyframes.
`cameraStation` fits a 16:9 camera box around focus ids, clear of the 83 % caption keep-out.
`ScriptSchema` parses a two-track `script/v1` script (with optional layer, framing, anchor, scene, structure and signature-layer fields),
`parseScript` also rejects a `structure` the registry lacks,
`deriveEvalView` derives the view evals read from it, and
`migrateTourV0` lifts a spike tour to v1.
`emptyStageRuns` fails a beat whose stage area holds no non-decor content box for more than 3 s of measured moments.
`contentFillFindings` fails a beat whose settled element boxes span less than 60 % of the frame width.
`cutCells` cuts beat-aware contact-sheet stills from beat bounds, measured cue times and beat kind (or the page's marks), stable when a beat is lengthened.
`explainer sheets` (`writeContactSheets`) tiles those stills, each with a label strip, into one PNG per chapter.
`scriptSha` names a script by its canonical-JSON sha, and
`explainer eval l0` runs the L0 checks and appends `structure.tsv` and `runs.jsonl` rows that carry `rules_sha`.
For an owner's blind read, `prepareOwnerSession` writes two-track storyboards under a sealed key and
`recordOwnerSession` appends `owner.tsv` rows before it opens the key.
`loadRuleRegistry` reads the shipped Q-rule registry (`doctrine/rules.yaml`), and
`unimplementedL0Rules` reports rules that claim a check no registered L0 check emits.
`loadDoctrine` reads the craft doctrine registry (`doctrine/craft/*.yaml` with its vocabulary and evidence ledger), and
`checkDoctrine` reports missing evidence ids, grades the cited rows do not state, live code-checked rules left in a prompt enforcement, unresolved `qrule` refs and scope errors.
`sliceForStage` returns the craft rules one pipeline stage loads for a video type, audience and beats (prompt, base and packet prose, checks, token names, profile params), never a code-enforced rule in prose, and
`findPromptLeaks` flags a prompt that names a code-enforced doctrine rule or an implemented-L0 Q-rule by id, alias or text.
`loadProfiles` reads the type profiles (`doctrine/types/*.yaml`: repo-tour, the explain-repo default, plus repo-argument, pr-overview, paper-summary and daily-overview) and audience packs.
`profileFor` rejects an unknown type,
`checkProfiles` reports vocabulary, structure, series (`mayRepeat` / `mustVary`), publish-guard and beat-system binding issues,
`chapterOrder` gives a fixed order for the tour and, for the others, the first heuristic row whose registered structure fits the material.
`loadStructures` reads the narrative structure registry (`doctrine/structures/*.yaml`: fifteen structures, each with a fit predicate over material signals, airtime shares and its own spine sections),
`structureFor` rejects an unknown structure, and
`checkStructures` reports vocabulary, signal, share and block issues.
`loadBeatSpecs` reads the beat-spec registry (`doctrine/beats/*.yaml`, one per vocabulary beat, each naming a zod slot schema in `BEAT_SLOTS` and an emphasis contract of target lists and template treatments),
`beatSpecFor` rejects an unknown beat,
`parseBeatSlots` rejects bad slots and duplicate emphasis ids,
`cueElement` resolves a cue target to exactly one emphasis element, and
`fillScript` maps each template beat of a script/v1 and its resolved row to slot props its spec's schema accepts (derived < resolver slots < `visual.slots`), falling back to a list it records and listing every refusal in a `FillError`,
`checkBeatSpecs` reports vocabulary, slot-ref, duration, recipe-length and emphasis-target issues.
`chartFrameProblems` refuses a chart or replot slot set with bars off a zero baseline or on a broken axis, a colour scale whose lightness (`lightness`, CIELAB L*) is out of order (`isMonotonicScale`), or a legend where direct labels fit, behind the resolve `chart-integrity` gate.
`loadBeatSystems` reads the beat-system registry (`doctrine/beat-systems/*.yaml`: nine ordered beat patterns, such as the CL order and BLUF, that a profile binds inside a structure's blocks) and rejects a system or step beat outside the vocabulary,
`beatSystemFor` rejects an unknown system, and
`placeBeatSystem` lands a system's steps in order in a profile's blocks.
`loadStylePacks` reads the style packs (`doctrine/style-packs/*.yaml`: four selections of existing titan-design tokens by slot) and rejects a pack naming a token outside the pinned `tokens.css` names, the wrong kind of token for a slot, or a channel whose look it would copy,
while each profile names the packs it allows and its voice band (Kokoro voice id and rate), and a render variant's `stylePack` puts the pack's content hash in the render key.
For a `sim` beat, a `SimModel` in `SIM_MODELS` simulates from the seed's generator only (`runPure` refuses `Math.random` and clocks with `SimPurityError`),
`sweepSim` runs it over one swept param and an optional facet with a seed per point, and
`freezeSim` seals the runs as an `explainer.sim-trace/v1` trace (`SimTraceSchema`) keyed by its canonical-JSON sha256.
`loadSims` reads the sim-model registry (`doctrine/sims/*.yaml`) and
`checkSims` reports a model with no doctrine file, a file with no model, and a doctrine statistic the model never emits.
`simCheck` passes a sim beat only when its run reproduces a gathered number fact within the doctrine tolerance, refusing a tolerance under 3 se, over a tenth of the claim, or on a fitted statistic, and
`runSimPass` sweeps, freezes and checks every sim beat at resolve, which cuts the failing ones before tts behind the `sim-cut-orphan` gate.
`reviewRounds` is the pilot model (`review-rounds`: round 1 passes with chance p1, later rounds with chance q, emitting mean reviews and the 5+ share, refusing a q under `MIN_LATER_PASS` or a prs over `MAX_REVIEW_PRS`), and
`fitLaterRoundPass` solves q from a gathered 5+ share, which the doctrine lists in `fittedFrom`.
`explainer guide types` writes each type's planner guide to `doctrine/guides/planner/<type>.md`.
`explainer eval l1` and `l2` run the L1 judge and L2 viewer through a configured claude-print or codex judge, void any score without a verbatim quote, plant canaries in every call, and key rows by an `eval_version` over rubric, judge and fixtures.
For pace evals, `fromScriptV1` and `fromSpikeScript` project a script to `PaceBeat`s (the items each beat puts on screen, their role from `CUE_KIND_ROLES`, and which are new),
`readSpikeScript` reads a Python-emitted spike script.json loosely and lists the fields it ignores, and
`readTiming` reads heard durations from a words.json.
`runCold` streams that track to a cold viewer one chapter per call, carrying only its three-line summary, and reports undefined items per chapter minute from generated questions scored against verbatim quotes.
`explainer eval cold` runs it three times by default and appends its rows and run records under an `eval_version` that includes the judge.
`paceCheck` (in `L0_CHECKS`) and `paceRows` lint that item track: Q-E7 at most 4 new items a beat (error), and as warnings Q-E8 seconds a new item, Q-E9 15 s to digest between dense beats and Q-E10 new items a chapter minute (`chapterPace`).
It also lints seating and reuse: Q-E11 a beat that states an invariant needs a map and states at most one (error),
Q-E13 `reuseFindings` names reused `origin: v2` beats that fail Q-E7, Q-E8, Q-E9 or Q-E11 with their heard seconds to re-voice, and
Q-E12 (`seatRoutes`) and Q-E14 (`explainRoutes`) only route beats to the L1 judges and never gate.
`runItems` is that L1 item judge: one call per chapter over `itemRoutes` (explain, seat and list routes, nothing else), asking whether each routed item is explained, each routed beat seated, and which listed item is the odd one out;
it voids any verdict without a verbatim quote, plants a name-only canary beat per call, and
`explainer eval items` runs it three times by default under eval id `L1-items`.
`varietyScriptCheck` (in `L0_CHECKS`) adds the script-only variety lints as warnings: `variety:hook-formula`, `variety:connector-share` (over 30 % of beats opening on so, but, then, and or now), `variety:cue-action` (one cue action across the script) and `variety:framing-run` when beats author `visual.framing`; `resolvedVarietyRows` holds the resolver's choices to the profile's component, template and framing limits at `checks:resolve`.
`explainer eval pace` runs only those lints on a spike or script/v1 file, with heard durations from `--timing`, appends their rows and prints items a minute per chapter, then the reused beats to re-voice when there are any.
To calibrate checks against labels, `LabelsSchema` parses a `labels/v1` labelled set (the v4 one is `fixtures/spike/redesign-explainer-v4/labels.json`) and
`calibrate` scores structure rows against it: precision and recall per check, with borderline labels counting as neither, and recall on the owner-named beats over error-severity rows.
`explainer eval calibrate` prints that report.
For a repo explainer, `gatherReview` reads a finished repo review (pinned clone, final label, `unread=0`) into a `review-bundle/v1` and schema-checked `ExplainerFact`s, tour kinds included (plus docs-skim and lifetime-history facts when the review has them), and refuses with coded diagnostics (`GATHER_CODES`) rather than throwing.
`renderCompanion` renders a repo run's companion doc (the martini-glass bowl) from those facts, one section per repo-tour block (`COMPANION_SECTIONS`), with each chapter's link into it and warnings rather than throws (`W-NO-SUMMARY`).
`companionChapters` maps script chapters to the blocks their spine rows play, so a digest cut links into the tour's doc; the script stage writes both as `companion` and `chapter-links`.
`enrichStructure` then adds the code structure: a `structure/v1` with repo-map levels, code-read centrality and reading order, entry points and code-graph call paths as map flows, and each fact's `centrality`, `reading_rank` and `module`.
When the review index has no snapshot at the pin, the fresh index covers only the files the review read (`reviewScopeFiles`, `scopedSource`), so a vendored tree is neither parsed nor opened by the type checker, and `W-INDEX-SCOPE` says so when no review file list exists and the whole clone is indexed.
For a PR video, `gatherPr` writes the pr-overview profile's `facts.jsonl` from the PR diff, its reviews and comments (through `gh`) and the code-graph calls between changed files at the head commit, with stable content-derived ids and coded refusals (`PR_GATHER_CODES`).
`explainer pr trigger` (`runPrVideoTrigger`, `autoBriefTargets`) starts a decision-brief run (the `gather` stage, then the audition;
with `--through script`, the script too, on the spine the audition writes from its pick, `pickSpine`, as pr-overview's `spine: { from: audition-pick }` declares)
only for PRs Shepherd holds at the owner's visual gate (`visual-gate2`) on a head still current right before the start, with `--dry-run`, and
`explainer pr gather` runs it on request.
For the daily briefing, `gatherDaily` reads one UTC day into a `digest.json` and a `facts.md` whose ids come from their sources
(PRs through `gh pr list`, sessions through `session-read`,
task deltas from `readTaskSnapshot`, which snapshots an active-work initiative read-only and reports tasks `opened`, `closed`, `moved` or `owner-gated` against the latest earlier snapshot).
`explainer run --facts-from gatherDaily --type daily-overview` starts a run from it
(as the run's `gather` stage with `--from gather`;
`gatherArticle` takes `--article` and `--claims`), and
`--dry-run` stops before any stage.
To make a whole video and see where its cost and time go, `explainer run` (`runVideo`) runs the `explainer-video` workflow:
an optional audition that writes `material-map.json` (deterministic signals from the facts and the fit predicates each structure reads, per profile; `--from audition --profile <type>`) and
`audition.json` (k spines from one verbalized-sampling call with stated likelihoods, each scored by code on fit, coverage, tension, range and freshness and by the reported-only cold-viewer rubric,
the agent's pick with its margin and runner-up, the profile's fixed order as the 0-candidate fallback, and no render),
script, rewrite, eval and TTS in process
(TTS: speech-tts Kokoro with strict words in the profile's voice band,
each beat calibrated to its speech band's words a minute from `doctrine/speech-bands.yaml`,
trued beat lengths,
`words.json` with absolute word times,
`voice.json`, and
a per-beat take cache),
then the render stage in process (`runRenderStage`: the template fill to a storyboard under beat-NN ids from `storyboardIds`, `compileTimeline`, the composition page with the style pack's CSS, `renderVideo` behind the run type's gate profile, a `duration-agreement` gate over the manifest and a reported `two-run` check, behind a `RenderEngine` seam),
then the qa stage in process (`runQaStage`: render-qa's gate at the cue moments and the 2 Hz sweep in Chromium behind a `QaEngine` seam, the `doctrine/qa/gate-profile.yaml` verdict through `loadQaGate`, the probe and framediff behind the motion-happened, clipped-text, content-fill and stage-empty checks, the DIRECTION timing gates of `timing-gates.ts` with thresholds from the type profile's `pacing`, render-qa's `mediaScan` behind the reported black-frames, silence-2s and frozen-frames checks, and `qa.json` as `explainer.qa/v1` with findings by beat and anchor),
then the sheets stage in process (`runSheetsStage`: ffprobe and ffmpeg through `ffmpegMedia`, `buildSidecar` for the theater's `video-meta@1` sidecar with an `explainer` block of video id, run ids, profile, script sha and fingerprint, and the poster),
`fingerprintOf` and `layoutKey` give each beat its `component/slots/anchors` layout key for the variety lints,
then a hard-linked export to the theater;
every stage but export is its own `explainer.<stage>` child workflow behind a stage cache keyed on the input shas it reads, its settings and variant file, and a sample index;
resolve builds each `layer: "custom"` beat's layer through claude-print by default, behind an esbuild compile gate and import allowlist, repairs a layer that fails the gate in one agent-chat round priced from the agent's transcript (when the host passes a repairer), and reuses an earlier run's build of an unchanged packet,
`explainer stage` runs one stage from stored shas,
`--from`/`--to`/`--pin` start and stop mid-pipeline,
`--budget-usd` is a resumable hard stop,
follow-up runs join the same video, and
`explainer run report [--compare <runId>]` writes `run-report.md` with per-stage wall time, usd, tokens, retries, cache hits, output shas and the video's linked-run total.
For an owner edit of a finished run, `SlotEditSchema` parses an `explainer.slot-edit/v1` (slot and tune fields per template beat, over a base run's script and render), and
`applyEdit` applies it to the base script, refusing a stale base, an unknown or custom-layer beat and a slot change that drops an element a cue targets, and returns the new script and a field diff.
`explainer edit check` prints that verdict with the slot-overrides gate, the template fill and the emphasis-target gate, and writes nothing,
`explainer edit apply [--start]` stores the script and the ledger row `<dataDir>/edits/<editId>.json` and launches the linked run from resolve (script and custom layers pinned, a $0.25 backstop), and
`explainer edit list` lists a render's or a video's edits with their linked run's status.
`explainer props --mp4-sha <sha>` reads the run that exported a render and gives each kept template beat its slot JSON Schema, filled value with overrides, overridden fields, cue-locked ids, span and still time, plus whether a save can change the render (it can, now render draws from the fill).
`compileTimeline` turns a storyboard and an optional words.json (its only reader) into the page's `timeline.json`: heard durations or planned ones with `provisional: true`, beat-local cue seconds for `word` or `word#n`, and slots parsed by `BEAT_SLOTS` until `@titan-design/beats` publishes; `writeTimeline` writes it as canonical JSON.
`renderVideo` renders a served `__titanMotion` page for a `RenderTimeline` through `@titan-design/frame-capture` to `<stem>.mp4` (H.264 + AAC), `captions.vtt` and `render-manifest.json`,
mixing narration with `mixAudio` or, with none, a sample-exact `silentMix` and `draft: true`.
`assertDurationAgreement` refuses a page and mix whose lengths differ by more than `DURATION_TOLERANCE_S`; `renderVideo` then deletes the mp4 and writes no manifest.
`renderVideo` with `qa: { mode: "gate" }` runs render-qa's cue-moment gate (`src/qa/cue-gate.ts`, shared with the qa stage) before mixing; held errors write `qa.json` and throw `QaRefused`, leaving no mix, mp4 or manifest.
`RenderManifestSchema` is `explainer.render-manifest/v1`: workers, frames, durations, draft, `qaGate` (`absent` with no `qa` option, `passed` with `qa: { heldErrors: 0, gateProfile }`, or `skipped`), a strict `RenderHostSchema` host with no hostname or paths (`collectRenderHost`), and the timeline, page, mix, mp4, vtt and words shas.
`toVtt` and `captionCues` write WebVTT from timed words (42 characters or 8 words a cue, broken at sentence ends, held 0.3 s).

<a id="cap-factory"></a>

### `factory`

Tier product, private, `products/factory`. Code-driven software-factory workflows: durable runs, routed step runners, evidence and gate-policy seams

**Use this when:**

You want code, not a coordinating agent, to own a software workflow's transitions, retries, human gates and evidence, and to resume it after a crash. The engine is `workflow`; this product holds the policy, the step router and the pilots. It requests agent dispatch through agent-chat, via `@titan-design/agent-dispatch`, for five kinds of agent: the Shepherd reviewer, the main-red fixer, the successor implementer, and build-surface's slice implementer and slice reviewer. It also starts one process that is not an agent, the detached deployer. Relay and agent-chat keep every other dispatch.

- **Reviewer.** Spawned when a registered pull request needs an independent review of its current head, and resumed for a later head. It runs under the agent-chat profile set by `review.profile` in the factory config (the profile is its tool grant) and under `review.configDir` when set, else agent-chat's default account. It starts in the repo's configured checkout, reads the head at that exact commit, changes nothing, and ends its final message with `Verdict: MERGE|FIX_FIRST`, `PR:` and `Head:` lines. After a FIX_FIRST on a repeat round it also names the defect class.
- **Fixer.** Spawned once per red-main episode, when main CI goes red after a merge and Shepherd freezes merges into the repo. Shepherd files a high-severity fix task in active-work first, and the fixer is named for the episode so a retry never starts a second one. It runs headless under the `bd-implementer` profile and under `shepherd.fixer.configDir` when set, else agent-chat's default account. It branches from main, opens a PR, registers it with Shepherd against the fix task, and ends with a `Head: <full sha>` line. Only that PR may merge while the freeze holds. With no agent-chat configured, nothing is spawned and the owner gets the red main.
- **Successor.** Spawned when Shepherd must wake an implementer (CI red, FIX_FIRST review, conflict, or a failed fix-proof check) and no agent of that lineage is live or resumable. A live implementer is messaged and an exited one is resumed; neither is a new dispatch. The successor runs headless under the `bd-implementer` profile and under `shepherd.fixer.configDir` when set, else agent-chat's default account. It continues on the PR's head branch, does not open a new PR, registers as the PR's implementer, and ends with a `Head: <full sha>` line.
- **Deployer.** Not an agent and not an agent-chat dispatch. After a merge into the factory's own repo, Shepherd starts `service deploy` for the merge sha as a detached process that outlives the service, and skips it if the service already runs that sha. It reports only through its log file in the state directory. Merges into any other repo start no deployer.
- **Build-surface implementer.** Spawned once per slice of a `build-surface` run (`titan-factory build-surface start <owner/repo> --spec <path>`), under the profile the repo's build spec names (`bd-implementer` by default), with `--role implementer` and the slice's task on its roster row. It starts in the spec's clone, works on the slice branch the workflow created, pushes, and ends its final message with a fenced JSON report that the workflow reads from its transcript. Each fix round resumes the same session, and the PR is registered with Shepherd under its name, so Shepherd's wake and successor logic follow that lineage.
- **Build-surface reviewer.** Spawned per gated head of a slice under the spec's read-only reviewer profile, with `--role reviewer`, never in the implementer's lineage. It reviews that exact head, changes nothing, and ends with a fenced JSON verdict that a validator checks before it counts.
- **Audit steps.** Not an agent-chat dispatch. Each agent step of `measurement-audit` (`titan-factory audit <area>`) is one `claude -p` turn through `@titan-design/agent`. The turn runs with no tools, on the CLI login, under the model the step's manifest names. It gets the inventory as data and answers with JSON that the step's schema checks.

- `config`: `FactoryConfigSchema`, `configPath`, `defaultDbPath`, `loadConfig`, `resolveDbPath`
- `definition`: `assertDistinctStepIds`, `declarationFor`, `defineWorkflow`, `dispatchStepIds`, `guardedContext`, `stepIdMatches`
- `evidence`: `evidenceRecord`

### `session-miner`

Tier product, private, `products/session-miner`. The session miner: index Claude Code transcripts into a session graph and serve it over CLI, MCP, and HTTP

**Use this when:**

<a id="cap-titan"></a>

### `titan`

Tier product, private, `products/titan`. The titan host CLI: health sampling of the factory and the host

**Use this when:**

You want this host's services sampled on a schedule and kept: `titan health sample` probes each target (by default the factory's loopback `/health`, with its pid file as identity), copies serve's own restart counters into the row, and writes every result plus a `self` row of the sampler's own CPU, fs blocks, context switches, RSS and wall time in one transaction. `titan health install` puts it on a minutely systemd user timer. `titan health uptime` reports up, down, unknown and missing slots, both up shares, the gaps and serve's restart and unclean-start deltas (with `--min` as a gate); `titan health cost` reports the sampler's per-tick cost and the store size; `titan health import` loads the old stopgap JSONL idempotently. `titan host doctor [--json]` runs the active-work, agent-chat and titan-factory doctors and reports each product and tool CLI's presence and version, warning when a linked product CLI differs from its checkout's package.json, then stats (never reads) every coordination inventory path for the platform, secrets included. `titan config report [--json]` lists this host's config surfaces as file facts (present, mode, mtime, size and sha256 for non-secrets), never values, and `--to` deposits them in the console's `config.report` over the LAN bearer. It makes no model or tool calls. The contract, probe, store and uptime fold live in the `health` package; to serve a health route, use daemon.

Key exports:

- `cli`: `runCli`, `CliIo`

<a id="cap-yt-scout"></a>

### `yt-scout`

Tier product, private, `products/yt-scout`. Scheduled AI-video scout: watch list, seen-set and video state for poll, transcribe, score and digest

**Use this when:**

You are working on the owner's scheduled AI-video scout (Y-15): the YouTube watch list (`WatchlistSchema`, `loadWatchlist`, line-numbered `WatchlistError`), the `videos` state table (`openScoutDb`, `VIDEO_STATES`) and the one-off seen-set import (`importSeen`), behind the `titan-yt-scout` CLI. Detect, transcribe and score are typed seams only (`Detector`, `Transcriber`, `Scorer`); full-text search over transcripts is `corpus-query`, and the durable step runner is `workflow`.

Key exports:

- `config`: `isOnTrial`, `SourceSchema`, `WatchlistSchema`
- `paths`: `configPath`, `dbPath`, `ytRoot`
- `seen-import`: `formatSeenImport`, `importSeen`, `mergeRecords`, `sourceResolver`
- `seen-sources`: `readSeenSources`
- `store`: `countByState`
- More in `products/yt-scout/src/index.ts`

<a id="cap-console"></a>

### `titan-console`

Tier product, private, `apps/console`. The titan console: one read-only loopback daemon and react-ui shell over active-work, the agent-chat broker and the session graph

**Use this when:**

You want a view over active-work, the agent-chat broker or the session graph: add it here as a route and a command, not as a new app or a new daemon. It is also the reference for a react-ui `AppShell` app served by one loopback daemon.

Key exports:

No library entry point.
